title: Technical English — Course 4, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 11

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the sensor lesson begin?
tasks.audioText: The electronics tutor will introduce sensor terminology on Tuesday at nine fifteen. Students should meet in the instrumentation classroom and bring the illustrated sensor chart. The lesson will compare temperature, light and proximity sensors and explain what each type detects. The class will use diagrams and recorded examples rather than live equipment.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which reference chart should students use for the sensor exercise?
tasks.audioText: The electronics tutor will introduce sensor terminology on Tuesday at nine fifteen. Students should meet in the instrumentation classroom and bring the illustrated sensor chart. The lesson will compare temperature, light and proximity sensors and explain what each type detects. The class will use diagrams and recorded examples rather than live equipment.

tasks.prompt: A temperature sensor provides information about temperature changes in a system. A light sensor responds to the level of light, while a proximity sensor can detect the presence of an object without direct contact. The output and operating range depend on the sensor model. A technician should check the data sheet before interpreting a signal or comparing different sensors. Reading 1. What can a proximity sensor detect?
options: The distance travelled by a moving component
The temperature of an object through direct contact
The presence of an object without direct contact
The electrical power supplied to a motor

tasks.prompt: Where should a technician check the operating range?
The sensor output ___ in the technical data sheet.
Choose TWO types of sensors and their typical purposes.
options: Proximity sensor — measures room temperature only
Light sensor — identifies a part number
Light sensor — responds to light level

tasks.prompt: A document that gives technical information about a component is a data ___.
You need to compare two sensor models. What should you check?
options: Could we compare their data sheets and operating ranges?
The model numbers are not useful.
I will assume their outputs are identical.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of sensor terminology in a logical order.
options: Identify the quantity or condition to detect
Record the output and operating range
correctOrder: Identify the quantity or condition to detect
Record the output and operating range

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words comparing two types of sensors. Describe what each detects and explain why the data sheet is important.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: two sensor types are identified and what each detects is described (0–2); the response explains why data-sheet information such as range, accuracy or output is needed to interpret the sensor correctly (0–2); the comparison is clear with understandable grammar (0–2); sensor/electronics vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are accurate (0–2).
